predecessors.name: Masaesyli
predecessors.text: Syphax's Masaesyli kingdom in the west (capital Siga), given to Masinissa after Zama in 202 BC; the Massylii kingdom at Cirta was Masinissa's own

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: eastern Numidia, annexed in 46 BC as the Roman province Africa Nova

ledger.x: 202 BC: Masinissa becomes first king of a united Numidia.
202 BC: Masinissa receives Syphax's kingdom after Zama.
By 158 BC: Masinissa holds the Tripolitanian coast.
146: Carthage is destroyed and the border war ends with it.
116: Rome partitions Numidia between Jugurtha and Adherbal.
112: Jugurtha takes Cirta and reunites the kingdom.
105: Bocchus I gets western Numidia for betraying Jugurtha.
46: Caesar annexes Numidia as Africa Nova after Juba I's defeat and death.
46: the kingdom ends with Juba I, who 'reigned from 60 to 46 BC' and died in 46 after the African campaign (he fled the field at Thapsus, then took his own life in a suicide pact with Petreius).

wars.name: Numidian-Carthaginian border war
wars.outcome: Masinissa seizes Carthaginian territory in 152, invades in 151 (Oroscopa) and defeats the Carthaginians; Carthage's war on Numidia breaches its treaty with Rome and leads to the Third Punic War.

wars.name: Jugurthine War
wars.outcome: Rome fights Jugurtha 112-105 (Bestia's peace, Albinus' surrender in 110, Metellus 109, Marius from 107); Bocchus I of Mauretania hands Jugurtha to Sulla in 105 and annexes the western part of the kingdom.

wars.name: Caesar's Civil War in Africa
wars.outcome: Juba I defeats Curio (August 49), joins Scipio, flees from Thapsus and dies in 46; Bocchus II and Publius Sittius invade Numidia from the west; Numidia becomes Africa Nova.
